slides.say: A lab report has weight five and a quiz has weight one. A student scores ninety-one on the lab report and fifty-five on the quiz. What is the weighted course score?
at: A lab report has weight five

slides.say: So it's a weighted average of two scores, and the lab report is five times heavier.
We'll solve it in two different ways. First by understanding with the seesaw, the way we'd do it on the exam. Then the math way, with the formula.
Let's start with the seesaw. We draw a line. Fifty-five and ninety-one go above its ends, and the weights go below, one and five.

slides: The lab report is five times heavier, so the average is five times closer to it. The weights are five to one, so the distances are one to five.

slides.say: We cut the gap into five plus one, six units.
The gap is ninety-one minus fifty-five, thirty-six. Thirty-six divided by six is six. So each unit is six.
The heavy side gets the small part, one unit. Ninety-one minus six is eighty-five.
Careful with sixty-one, choice number three. That's one unit from fifty-five, the light side.
So the score is eighty-five. That's choice number two.
[pause] Now the math way, with the formula. We start again from the givens. Each score times its weight, divided by the sum of the weights.
Ninety-one times five. Ninety times five is four hundred fifty, and five more is four hundred fifty-five.
Plus fifty-five times one. Four hundred fifty-five plus fifty-five is five hundred ten.
The weights add up to five plus one, six.
Five hundred ten divided by six. Four hundred eighty divided by six is eighty. And thirty divided by six is five. So it's eighty-five.
at: Four hundred eighty divided by six

slides.say: Choice number two is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number two is our answer
